- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or shows sharp decline, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to account for risk-off or panic-driven rebounds.  
- After a price spike (forecast > 72), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward correction at 5% of spike magnitude to avoid overshoot.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 68), model often fails to recognize it; apply a 2–4% upward bias to counteract downward drift.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply a 1–2% downward adjustment to first 5 days.  
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from +0.8 to -0.3), model often lags; adjust forecast 1–3 days ahead to reflect sentiment shift.
